statement: Crate doc declares the Entrybound Archive Model (EAM) authoritative; ECF is only an encoding of it, indexes are caches, and the CLI consumes the library rather than re-implementing archive semantics.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with SPEC §3.1 L129-130 (EntrySet authoritative)

statement: Public modules: archive, chunker, crypto, diagnostics, eam, ecf, identity, legacy, planner, random_access, similarity. Crate-private modules: canonical, codec, jpeg_reconstruction, reconstruction, transform.

Canonical TLV encoding, codec encode/decode, transforms and reconstruction are crate-private; no public API lets an external harness encode one payload with a codec, run a transform, or serialize one canonical record without building a whole archive.
research_needed: Determine which experiments (codec portfolio, manifest size) need direct access; measure overhead of going through ecf::encode
decision_needed: Should a research-only cargo feature expose canonical/codec/transform internals, or must experiments use whole-archive encode?

statement: The eam module is documented as 'the supported Entrybound Archive Model subset': the code implements a bootstrap subset, not the full architecture EAM.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §3 EAM to a bootstrap subset
research_needed: Enumerate every SPEC §3 object/field missing from the subset
decision_needed: Which missing EAM elements are V1-blocking versus deferrable?

statement: Public EAM re-exports include LogicalPath/PathComponent/PathEncoding, Archive, ArchiveDescriptor, ArchiveRole, Chunk, ChunkGroup, ContentObject, ContentStore, Dictionary, Entry/EntryKind/EntrySet, MetadataItem/MetadataSet, FidelityReport, Index, Layout, ResourceBudget, TransformPlan, reconstruction and legacy-preservation types.
PathEncoding has a single variant, Utf8 (without normalization). No utf16le, legacy(charset), or NFC/NFD encoding declarations exist.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §3.4 L203-208 declared encodings to UTF-8 only
research_needed: Survey legacy corpora (ZIP CP437, tar non-UTF-8 names) to size the population needing non-UTF-8 declarations
decision_needed: Is UTF-8-only path encoding acceptable for v1, and how are non-UTF-8 source names represented?

statement: A PathComponent must be non-empty and contain neither NUL nor '/' bytes; violations are NONCONFORMING with EB_EAM_INVALID_PATH_COMPONENT.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §3.4 P3 / §11.2 L1345 (no separator confusion)
research_needed: Add a test asserting EB_EAM_INVALID_PATH_COMPONENT (no test asserts this code)

statement: Components whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 are refused as UNSUPPORTED; the message states the bootstrap subset requires valid UTF-8 components.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §10.8 L1307 (exact filename bytes plus declared encoding)
research_needed: Measure frequency of non-UTF-8 filenames on Linux trees and legacy archives
decision_needed: How will non-UTF-8 POSIX filenames be archived losslessly?

statement: Components exactly '.' or '..' are unrepresentable (NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_DOT_COMPONENT / EB_EAM_DOT_DOT_COMPONENT). A raw-byte check suffices only because UTF-8 is the sole encoding.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §3.4 P7 / I27 (Appendix A L2718) for UTF-8 only
research_needed: If more encodings are added, decoded-form dot checks (UTF-16 2E00 2E00) need tests

statement: A LogicalPath must contain at least one component; the type has no root, drive-letter or absolute form.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §11.2 L1344 (absolute paths unrepresentable)

statement: Canonical LogicalPath order compares component by component, first by component byte length then by bytes; a proper prefix sorts first. Example order: a, a/z, b, aa.
refines_or_supersedes: Realizes SPEC §3.4 L208 normative canonical order; exact rule to be checked against SPEC text
research_needed: Confirm SPEC §3.4 L208 defines length-then-bytes per component; cross-check with independent reader
decision_needed: Is the length-first component order frozen for identity/v1?

statement: LogicalPath imposes no per-component byte-length limit and no depth limit; depth is bounded only through ResourceBudget.max_path_depth at the container level.
research_needed: Measure/decide a component-length bound versus target filesystem limits (typically 255 bytes)
decision_needed: Should the model bound component length, or leave it to extraction policy?

statement: No P5 collision-class detection (case-fold, NFC/NFD, Windows reserved names, trailing dot/space) exists in the LogicalPath model; byte-distinct colliding paths are accepted without classification.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §3.4 P5 L228-230 requires collision detection and a descriptor summary
research_needed: Evaluate target-specific collision detectors (NTFS upcase tables, APFS, ext4 casefold)
decision_needed: Where is P5 detection implemented (model, writer warning, extractor) and which Unicode version is pinned?

statement: LogicalPath Display joins components with '/' for human output and errors if a component is not UTF-8; display form is not an identity input.
Digest is a fixed 32-byte value; the active algorithm is declared by the descriptor. Digest::ZERO is a placeholder used before identities are applied.
ArchiveRole has only the Complete variant (all content internal, independently extractable). Sidecar and Incremental roles do not exist.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §8.5 L957-961 (Complete, Sidecar, Incremental)
decision_needed: Are Sidecar and Incremental roles in V1 scope, and how are they bound into LAI?

statement: Layout is a physical/access-capability choice only: two archives encoding the same EAM under INDEXED and STREAM have identical LAI, PCR and AUX and differ only in PCI. STREAM has no Index; entry lookup needs a full scan.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md L409-416 layout equivalence

statement: Layout wire discriminants are INDEXED=1 and STREAM=2 with names 'INDEXED'/'STREAM'; only INDEXED supports random entry lookup.
EntryKind is exactly Directory, File, Symlink, ReparsePoint. Hardlinks are ordinary Files carrying auxiliary hardlink-group metadata.
refines_or_supersedes: Diverges from SPEC §3.3 L166-174 (Directory, File, Symlink, Fifo, Socket, BlockDevice, CharDevice); adds ReparsePoint, answering SPEC open question §3.3 (spec-01-0093)
decision_needed: Should SPEC §3.3 be amended to add ReparsePoint as an EntryKind?

statement: No EntryKind exists for FIFOs, sockets, block devices or character devices; such special files cannot be represented in the model.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §3.3 L166-174 freezes Fifo, Socket, BlockDevice, CharDevice as EntryKinds
research_needed: Measure prevalence of special files in backup/rootfs corpora and tar imports
decision_needed: Are special files V1 scope, and where do device major/minor numbers live?

statement: ContentRef supports only Internal(Digest) referencing an internal ContentObject by plaintext logical digest; there is no External {digest, length, locator} variant.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §15.4 L1722-1725 defines a two-variant ContentRef (Internal, External)
decision_needed: Is the External ContentRef variant (sidecars, incremental base chains) in V1 scope?

statement: TimestampPrecision values: Second, Centisecond, Microsecond, Hectonanosecond, Nanosecond.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §10.4 L1256

statement: Timestamp is signed i64 seconds plus u32 nanoseconds with explicit source precision and a restorable flag; nanoseconds >= 1e9 are NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §10.4 L1253-1265

statement: Timestamp carries no epoch/time-scale, leap-second or zone-less-local-time semantics, and its per-value restorable bool overlaps MetadataItem.restorability (e.g. macos.birthtime is CaptureOnly while its Timestamp may be restorable=true).
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC open questions §10.4 L1253-1258 and L1257 vs §10.1 L1199 remain unresolved in code
decision_needed: Which of Timestamp.restorable and MetadataItem.restorability is authoritative, and what epoch/time scale is normative?

statement: LinkTarget stores exact target bytes (not a LogicalPath) with one canonical encoding: valid UTF-8 must use UTF8, otherwise POSIX_BYTES; targets containing NUL are NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_SYMLINK_TARGET; UTF8 declared on invalid UTF-8 is refused.
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves SPEC open question §3.3 L180 (spec-01-0100) on target encoding

statement: Symlink targets larger than 1 MiB are POLICY_REFUSED as exceeding a 'format bound'; the 1 MiB value has no cited measurement (platform PATH_MAX/NTFS limits are far smaller).
research_needed: Survey platform symlink target limits (Linux 4096, Windows 16 KiB reparse buffer) and justify the bound
decision_needed: Should the symlink-target bound be tightened and moved to a registry of format limits?

statement: WindowsReparsePoint requires a nonzero tag and data at most 16 KiB minus 8 bytes (Windows complete reparse buffer limit, excluding tag/length/reserved header); oversize data is POLICY_REFUSED.
evidence_in_source: code (cites Windows 16 KiB limit); test model.rs:2166-2171

statement: ACL model: dialects POSIX1E and NFS4; scopes ACCESS and DEFAULT; entry types ALLOW, DENY, AUDIT, ALARM; principals USER_OBJ, USER(uid), GROUP_OBJ, GROUP(gid), MASK, OTHER, OWNER@, GROUP@, EVERYONE@, UUID.
ACL principals are numeric uid/gid or 16-byte UUID only; no string names (user@domain, Windows SIDs outside descriptors) or id_space are representable.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.5 L1280 requires id_space; identity/strict-v1 (SPEC §20.3 L2207) needs names
research_needed: Assess macOS/NFSv4 ACL name-based principals round-trip needs
decision_needed: Should ACL principals support names or id spaces for cross-host restore?

statement: AclEntry constants: POSIX read=1, write=2, execute=4, mask 0x7; NFS4 permission mask 0x001f01ff and flag mask 0xff per RFC 7530 ACE4 registry used for macOS mapping. AclEntry::new performs no validation itself.
An ACL must contain 1 to 65,536 entries (NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_ACL otherwise), and NFS4 ACLs may use only ACCESS scope in v1.
research_needed: Justify 65,536-entry bound against filesystem ACL limits

statement: POSIX1E ACL entries must be ALLOW with zero flags and only rwx bits, strictly ordered by principal key (USER_OBJ, USER, GROUP_OBJ, GROUP, MASK, OTHER), with exactly one USER_OBJ/GROUP_OBJ/OTHER and a MASK iff named entries exist.
NFS4 ACL entries retain semantically significant source order and may use only OWNER@/GROUP@/EVERYONE@/USER/GROUP/UUID principals with permissions and flags within the registered masks.

WindowsSecurityDescriptor stores exact self-relative bytes (20 bytes to 1 MiB): revision 1, SE_SELF_RELATIVE set, resource-manager byte only with its control bit, ACL presence flags matching offsets, components 4-byte aligned, non-overlapping, with no trailing bytes.
research_needed: Fuzz descriptor parser against real-world SDs from NTFS volumes

statement: SIDs must be revision 1 with at most 15 subauthorities; ACLs must be revision 2 or 4 with zero reserved bytes and ACE count/length exactly consuming the ACL.

Only ACE types 0x00-0x15 are accepted (basic, compound, object, callback, label/resource/filter families); any other ACE type or unknown object-presence flag makes the descriptor NONCONFORMING rather than preserved opaquely.
research_needed: Check whether future Windows ACE types exist or are planned; test real SACL/label ACEs
decision_needed: Should unknown ACE types be preserved as opaque bytes instead of refused?

statement: XAttr names must be 1-255 bytes and NUL-free (NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_XATTR); values above 16 MiB are POLICY_REFUSED as exceeding the format bound.
XAttr value bound of 16 MiB is chosen without cited measurement and exceeds the Linux kernel 64 KiB value limit noted in the architecture.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.7 L1294 cites 255-byte names and 64 KiB values
research_needed: Measure xattr sizes on macOS (resource forks via xattr can exceed 64 KiB) and Linux; justify 16 MiB
decision_needed: What xattr value bound is normative for v1?

statement: SparseMap holds logical size plus at most 1,000,000 extents; extents must be nonzero-length, ordered, non-overlapping, non-adjacent and in range (NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_SPARSE_MAP); too many extents are POLICY_REFUSED.
research_needed: Justify 1,000,000-extent bound

statement: A sparse map is an AUX-only topology declaration over full plaintext: declared holes must contain only zero bytes (a nonzero byte in a hole is CORRUPT), and the map's logical size must equal the content length.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts/refines SPEC §8.4 L953 ('no sparse map: holes are chunks'); resolves SPEC open question §10.7 L1302-1303 since the map is AUX-authenticated and checked against zero bytes
decision_needed: Should SPEC §8.4 be amended to admit a verified posix.sparse-map metadata item?

statement: MetadataName is a closed registry of 15 names (metadata versions 1-3): core.executable, core.mtime, posix.mode, posix.uid, posix.gid, posix.hardlink-group, posix.xattrs, posix.sparse-map, security.acls, windows.security-descriptor, windows.file-attributes, windows.creation-time, windows.reparse-original, macos.flags, macos.birthtime.

The metadata registry is closed: no open x- / reverse-DNS extension names, and no items for owner/group names, atime/ctime, Linux birth time, NTFS alternate data streams, resource forks/FinderInfo, origin/quarantine markers, SELinux labels or file capabilities.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.2 L1217-1223 (open x- namespaces), §10.5, §10.7 L1296, §11.7 L1447-1450 require these classes
research_needed: Prioritize missing metadata classes by prevalence and restore feasibility per platform
decision_needed: Which additional metadata names are V1 and is an extension namespace allowed?

statement: Only core.executable participates in identity v1; every other implemented metadata item (mtime, mode, uid/gid, hardlink group, xattrs, sparse map, ACLs, Windows/macOS metadata) is AUX-only.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §12.4 L1493-1495 (executable bit participates by default)

statement: Criticality has Optional and Critical variants, but every MetadataItem constructor sets Optional and fields are private, so Critical items cannot be created through the public API; the v3 decoder refuses non-default criticality (ecf/records.rs:1472-1476).
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.3 L1245 and §20.1 L2182-2184 require per-item criticality with refusal of unknown Critical items
decision_needed: How is the Critical bit exercised in v1 (which names are Critical) and what is the reader behavior for unknown Critical items?

statement: Restorability has only Restorable and CaptureOnly; there is no PlatformSpecific restore class.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.1 L1193-1201 lists Restorable, CaptureOnly, PlatformSpecific
decision_needed: Is PlatformSpecific needed for v1 items (e.g. namespaced Linux capabilities)?

statement: windows.file-attributes retains mask 0x005af9a7, excluding DIRECTORY, SPARSE_FILE and REPARSE_POINT bits because EntryKind and the native sparse/reparse models are their sole authorities; macos.flags retains mask 0x40bf80ef (stable UF_*/SF_* flags).
research_needed: Validate masks against current Windows and Darwin headers

statement: posix.mode silently masks the supplied value to 0o7777, discarding file-type bits.
posix.xattrs holds at most 4096 xattrs per entry (POLICY_REFUSED beyond), sorted by name then value, with unique names (NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_DUPLICATE_XATTR).
research_needed: Justify 4096 per-entry bound

statement: security.acls must be non-empty (an empty list is a forbidden alternate encoding), hold at most 3 ACLs per entry, and have unique (dialect, scope) pairs sorted canonically.
windows.file-attributes values with bits outside the platform-v1 mask are NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_WINDOWS_METADATA, and FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL (0x80) is valid only alone.
macos.flags values with reserved bits outside the platform-v1 mask are NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_MACOS_METADATA.
macos.birthtime is recorded as CaptureOnly while windows.creation-time and core.mtime are Restorable; restorability is fixed per name by constructors, not writer-chosen.
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves SPEC open question §10.1 vs §10.2a (spec-04-0135) for implemented names: no writer override
research_needed: Verify macOS birthtime restore feasibility (setattrlist) to confirm CaptureOnly

statement: MetadataSet is canonically sorted by name and each metadata name may appear at most once; duplicates are NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION.
MetadataSet::executable() returns false when core.executable is absent, so an absent item and an explicit false are indistinguishable to callers (though they differ in identity encoding).
research_needed: Check whether writers always emit core.executable so LAI does not depend on absent vs false
decision_needed: Must core.executable always be present for File entries?

statement: Feature-gating predicates: posix-metadata-v1 is used by any posix.* item or any Symlink entry; platform-security-metadata-v1 is used by any security/windows/macos item or any ReparsePoint entry.
Each Entry carries exactly two explicit digests: identity_digest (LAI-bearing) and aux_digest (AUX-bearing).
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §8.0 L871-872; supersedes single entry_id of SPEC §3.2 L160 (E2)

statement: EntryData is kind-specific (Directory, File{content}, Symlink{target}, ReparsePoint{value}), making a Directory carrying content structurally unrepresentable.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §11.2 L1352

statement: Entry is the sole authority for one archived object; Entry::new accepts arbitrary identity placeholders that identity::apply_native_identities later recomputes; replace_metadata is crate-private.
ContentObject = logical_digest, chunk_root, ordered ChunkRefs; Chunk = chunk_id, logical_len, plan_ref, optional group_ref, and retained plaintext bytes held in memory.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §3.5 L234-246

statement: The in-memory Archive model retains every unique Chunk's plaintext in BTreeMaps, so non-streaming creation/open paths scale with total unique content held in RAM.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS for INDEXED pack/open versus archive size; identify paths that avoid retention
decision_needed: Is beyond-RAM INDEXED creation/extraction a v1 requirement?

statement: Dictionary is a first-class shared codec dictionary addressed by its exact bytes (dictionary_id), with codec, format and construction strings.
ReconstructionData is physical side data identified by its exact bytes and never part of logical archive identity; it records format and intermediate length.

Reconstruction audits are non-authoritative planning records. Legacy fallback reasons: UnrecognizedOrVerificationFailed, CompleteCostDidNotWin. Frozen v6 whole-object reasons: NotRecognized, Unsupported, ExactVerificationFailed, CompleteCostDidNotWin, RegionDedupConflict, ResourcePolicyExcluded, targeting Chunk, ContentObject or Region.

ReconstructionRegion is one physical representation for a contiguous ContentObject chunk range; membership is authoritative only via content_object, start_chunk_index and chunk_count, with a declared worst-case RegionAccessCost.
ChunkGroup declares bounded dependency (group_id, max_lookback, max_preceding_bytes); membership exists only through Chunk.group_ref and CHUNK_DATA order supplies preceding-member order.
ContentStore.physical_order is the exact CHUNK_DATA frame order; it is physical only and never changes ContentObject reference order or any logical identity.

TransformPlan (plan_id, identifier, TransformSteps, codec, codec_params, optional dictionary, DecodeRequirements) is decoder-facing: the planner is not needed to decode. reconstruction_ref appears only on reconstructive steps. DecodeRequirements = window_bytes, working_set_bytes, flags.

FidelityReport has captured classes, unavailable and degraded FidelityIssues {class, reason, optional entry_scope}, a platform string, and a filesystem list; classes and reasons are free-form strings.
FidelityReport lacks degraded {from, to} fields, a closed MetadataClass vocabulary, structured source-platform description, and per-entry counts required by the architecture.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §10.9 L1313-1323 requires degraded {class, from, to, entry_scope} and SourcePlatformDescription
decision_needed: Should FidelityReport classes be a closed registry with from/to degradation fields?

statement: ConversionResolution/ConversionProvenance are auxiliary evidence describing how foreign observations were projected; never an authority for the resulting Entry or ContentObject. Provenance records source format, adapter id, source digest, import mode, counts (observation, omission, refinement, divergence, irreconcilable), resolutions, synthesized ancestors, unsupported metadata, outcome.

LegacyPreservation (preserve-v1) retains exact source bytes, ordered LOM observations (scope 0 archive-wide, 1 per source entry), conflicts with all competing observations, and selected resolutions; parser validity (Valid/Invalid/Uninterpreted) is frozen independently of reconciliation policy; compatibility profile stays in the adapter ID.
Index is a reconstructible, non-authoritative acceleration structure (present, valid, chunk locators, free-form status string).

FeatureSet is three u64 tiers (incompat, read_only_compat, compat); ResourceBudget has eight u64 fields: entry_count, total_logical_bytes, max_single_entry_logical_bytes, max_expansion_ratio_milli, chunk_count, max_path_depth, max_metadata_bytes, max_key_derivation_cost.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §4.2 eight declared bounds and three-tier bitmap

statement: IdentityProfile has only IdentityV1; identity/strict-v1 (mode bits, ownership names, mtime, hardlink group) is not implemented.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §8.3 L934 and §20.3 L2207 define identity/strict-v1
decision_needed: Is identity/strict-v1 required for v1, given no ownership-name metadata exists?

statement: DigestAlgorithm has a single variant, Sha256, described as the single digest selected by this experimental format version.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §25.1 row 7 L2539 (one algorithm per version) but not its preference for a tree-capable digest
research_needed: Benchmark SHA-256 vs BLAKE3 throughput and verified-range proof size
decision_needed: Is SHA-256 the frozen v1 digest, or is a tree-capable hash adopted before v1?

statement: ArchiveDescriptor carries format major/minor, namespace, features, layout, role, budget_declared, stream_dedup_window (always 0 in INDEXED), budget, decode requirements, identity profile, digest algorithm, planner_id, chunker_id, LAI, PCR, AUX and optional PCI.
ArchiveDescriptor has no path collision-class summary and no hostility-class summary.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §3.4 P5 L230 and §4.2 L384 require collision/hostility summaries
decision_needed: Are collision/hostility summaries still required given SPEC open question §3.4 (spec-01-0148) about single authority?

statement: Archive bundles descriptor, entry set, content store, transform plans, fidelity report, optional ConversionProvenance (None for native archives), optional LegacyPreservation, and a reconstructible Index.
EntrySet::new sorts input into canonical LogicalPath order, so entry enumeration order cannot affect the model (P4/P6 then validated).
EntrySet::from_canonical rejects equal adjacent paths as NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH (P4) and out-of-order entries as EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §3.4 P4 L216

statement: Every proper prefix of an Entry path must exist as a Directory entry: absence is EB_EAM_MISSING_ANCESTOR; a File, Symlink or ReparsePoint ancestor is EB_EAM_FILE_AS_ANCESTOR.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §3.4 P6 L218

statement: Archive::validate = validate_without_retained_plaintext + plaintext-length checks. STREAM readers use the plaintext-free entry point because they verify chunk digests on arrival and release plaintext; all other invariants are identical for both layouts.
Model validation refuses any archive whose role is not Complete as UNSUPPORTED EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE ('only Complete archives are supported by the bootstrap profile').
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §8.5 L957-961
decision_needed: Timeline for Sidecar/Incremental support?

statement: INDEXED archives must declare stream_dedup_window = 0; otherwise NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING.

The conversion-provenance-v1 incompat bit must be set iff ConversionProvenance is present; legacy-preservation-v1 must be set iff a preservation object is present and requires conversion-provenance-v1 (EB_ECF_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION otherwise).

Metadata feature consistency: posix-metadata-v1 required whenever POSIX semantics are used and refused when set without them (unless platform bit set); platform-security-metadata-v1 set iff platform semantics are used and requires posix-metadata-v1.
LegacyPreservation is valid only with format 'legacy-preservation/v1' and source_format 'ZIP'; preserve-mode evidence for tar, 7z or other formats is rejected (CORRUPT EB_INTEGRITY_AUX_MISMATCH).
decision_needed: Is --preserve required for tar/7z/compressed-stream imports in v1?

statement: Preservation integrity: SHA-256(source_bytes) must equal source_digest and the conversion source digest; selected resolutions must equal conversion resolutions; observations strictly ordered by (scope, subject, observation ordinal); conflicts by ordinal; scope in {0,1}; evidence extents within source; conflict authority/value/evidence cardinalities equal and nonzero.
TransformPlan IDs must be unique; every Dictionary referenced by a plan must exist (EB_EAM_UNKNOWN_DICTIONARY) and every stored Dictionary must be referenced (no orphans).
Every ReconstructionData referenced by a TransformStep must exist (EB_RECONSTRUCTION_DATA_UNKNOWN) and every stored ReconstructionData must be referenced.
physical_order must list every unique Chunk exactly once (a permutation of the chunk map); otherwise EB_ECF_INVALID_CHUNK_GROUP_ORDERING.
Dictionary map key must equal dictionary_id, and SHA-256 of dictionary bytes must equal dictionary_id (CORRUPT EB_INTEGRITY_DICTIONARY_DIGEST_MISMATCH).

ReconstructionRegion checks: identity recomputes from canonical physical fields (CORRUPT otherwise); ContentObject exists; representation 1 byte..64 MiB (MAX_JXL_BYTES); logical bytes at most 64x representation; chunk_count 1..4096 and within the object.
research_needed: Justify 64 MiB, 64x expansion and 4096-chunk region caps with corpus measurements

statement: A region's plan must be independent and self-contained (no dictionary, first step whole-object reconstructive); member Chunks must use REGION_MEMBER_PLAN_REF (0), carry no ChunkGroup, and belong to only one region.
Region access declaration must be consistent (logical bytes and chunk counts match, worst_reconstructed_bytes equals logical bytes) and regions within one ContentObject must not overlap.
ReconstructionAudit map key must equal its explicit target, transform_id must be non-empty, and the targeted Chunk, ContentObject or Region must exist.
ChunkGroup ids must be nonzero and equal the map key; stored groups must declare nonzero max_lookback (EB_CODEC_LOOKBACK_VIOLATION).

Chunk checks: key equals chunk_id; a region-member plan ref without a region is rejected when whole-object reconstruction is enabled; non-region chunks must reference an existing plan (UNSUPPORTED EB_EAM_UNKNOWN_TRANSFORM_PLAN); group_ref must name an existing group.

Fallback-audit validation uses .expect('Chunk plan reference was validated above'); a fallback keyed to a region-owned Chunk (plan_ref 0, skipped by the earlier plan check) with no plan 0 could panic instead of returning a typed diagnostic.
research_needed: Fuzz/craft an archive with both whole-object and reconstructive features, a region, and a fallback on a member chunk; confirm decoder rejects earlier or panics

statement: A Chunk cannot carry both a selected reconstruction (plan with reconstruction_ref) and a reconstruction fallback audit.

ContentObject map key must equal logical_digest, every referenced Chunk must exist (EB_EAM_UNKNOWN_CHUNK), and every File entry's ContentRef must name an existing ContentObject (EB_EAM_UNKNOWN_CONTENT_OBJECT).
With retained plaintext, each Chunk's logical_len must equal its plaintext length (NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_SECTION_STRUCTURE) and sparse holes are verified.
When both core.executable and posix.mode are present they must agree (executable iff any 0o111 bit set); disagreement is NONCONFORMING EB_EAM_INVALID_POSIX_METADATA.
research_needed: Add a conformance test for this reason code

statement: posix.sparse-map and posix.hardlink-group are valid only on File entries (EB_EAM_INVALID_SPARSE_MAP / EB_EAM_INVALID_HARDLINK_GROUP).

A hardlink group needs at least two File members sharing one ContentObject and identical non-group metadata (inode-scoped: mode, owner, mtime, xattrs, ACLs); the stored group id must equal the canonical hardlink_group_id (CORRUPT otherwise).
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves SPEC open question §3.3/§3.3a (spec-01-0103): group ids are canonical and inode-independent; hardlinked special files (SPEC §3.3a L189) unsupported

statement: DEFAULT-scope ACLs are valid only on Directory entries; a POSIX1E ACCESS ACL requires posix.mode and must agree with it (owner=USER_OBJ, group=MASK or GROUP_OBJ, other=OTHER).
refines_or_supersedes: Relates to SPEC §10.6 L1289 chmod/ACL mask interaction

statement: windows.reparse-original metadata is valid only on Symlink entries (EB_EAM_INVALID_REPARSE_POINT).

Aggregate platform/security metadata size is estimated as 32 bytes per ACL entry plus security-descriptor bytes plus reparse data, and must not exceed a nonzero max_metadata_bytes; xattrs and other metadata are not counted here. A zero budget is an in-memory pre-serialization sentinel.
research_needed: Confirm the ECF writer's exact canonical metadata bound covers xattrs; validate the 32-byte ACL-entry estimate
decision_needed: Should max_metadata_bytes enforcement in the model cover all metadata, and is zero-as-sentinel acceptable?

statement: Sparse-hole validation walks every chunk of the File's ContentObject: sparse logical size must equal summed chunk lengths and all bytes in declared holes must be zero.

Every declared ChunkGroup must have at least two physical members forming one contiguous run in CHUNK_DATA order, and max_preceding_bytes must exactly equal the computed maximum preceding logical bytes within max_lookback (CORRUPT EB_ECF_ACCESS_COST_MISMATCH).
total_logical_size sums chunk lengths per File entry, so content shared by several entries (hardlinks, duplicates) is counted once per entry; this value is bound into LAI.
canonical.rs is the central canonical record/TLV encoding for ecf/bootstrap-v1: 16-byte record header, 12-byte field header, record versions 1-3, and a 1,000,000-item sequence cap.
Canonical field types: U8=1, U16=2, U32=3, U64=4, I64=5, Bool=6, Bytes=7, Utf8=8, Sequence=9; any other type byte is NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING.

Record version 2 is assigned only to Descriptor (kind 1), Entry (3) and MetadataItem (8); version 3 only to Entry and MetadataItem. The ordinary constructor stays frozen at version 1 for historical writers; other kind/version pairs are refused.
Field tags must be strictly increasing: a repeated tag is NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION and a decreasing tag EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING, both when building and decoding.

Record bytes: kind u16 BE, version u16 BE, flags u32 zero, payload length u64 BE, then fields (tag u16 BE, type u8, flags u8 zero, length u64 BE, value). Sequences: count u64 BE then per item length u64 BE and bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md L15-24 and L364
research_needed: Measure manifest overhead from 12-byte field and 16-byte record headers with u64 lengths per entry
decision_needed: Is fixed u64 length framing acceptable for manifest size targets?

statement: Decoders reject any field tag not in the record's required/optional set as NONCONFORMING (unknown bootstrap field tag); unknown fields are never skipped, so evolution happens only via record versions or feature bits.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §20.2 L2196 fail-closed on unknown critical features

statement: Record decoding: a header shorter than 16 bytes or a payload length beyond enclosing bytes is CORRUPT EB_ECF_SECTION_STRUCTURE; version 0, >3 or misassigned is NONCONFORMING; nonzero record flags are NONCONFORMING.
At record level, truncated headers and lengths exceeding enclosing bytes are classified CORRUPT (SectionStructure), never TRUNCATED; distinguishing truncation depends on outer container checks.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §19.4 L2154 requires truncated/corrupt/unsupported to stay distinguishable
research_needed: Test truncated archives at record boundaries in INDEXED and STREAM to confirm TRUNCATED class is reported

statement: Fixed-width fields must have their exact minimal width, booleans must be 00 or 01, and UTF-8 fields must be valid UTF-8; violations are NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_NONCANONICAL_ENCODING.
Sequences declaring more than 1,000,000 items are POLICY_REFUSED as 'bootstrap policy'; the cap is not derived from any measurement and is not caller-configurable.
research_needed: Check whether large archives (e.g. >1M chunk refs in one ContentObject) hit this cap
decision_needed: Should the sequence cap be a caller policy or a declared budget field?

statement: A sequence's items must exactly consume its field: truncated counts or item lengths are CORRUPT, trailing bytes are NONCONFORMING.
Lengths that do not fit the platform usize are POLICY_REFUSED EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT, so 32-bit readers refuse large fields rather than mis-parse.
decode_record_stream decodes a concatenation of canonical records until input is exhausted.
RecordBuilder, decode_record and FieldType are pub(crate); an independent research harness cannot construct or parse canonical records without a feature flag or re-implementation.
decision_needed: Expose canonical codec behind a research feature to support an independent-reader differential harness?

statement: Chunk and ContentObject logical digests are SHA-256 over exact plaintext; structured digests are SHA-256('Entrybound hash v1\0' || u64 domain length || domain || u64 field count || each u64 length || field).
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md L370-385; realizes SPEC I22 descriptor-binding

statement: BOOTSTRAP_CHUNK_SIZE = 1 MiB fixed chunking used only by direct in-memory construction; STORE_PLAN_ID = 1 with identifier 'bootstrap-store-v1' and codec 'store/v1'.
Four identities: LAI, PCR, AUX (computable before container bytes exist, NativeRoots) and PCI (SHA-256 over every exact serialized container byte, combined afterwards via with_pci).
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §8.0 L879-883 three signed roots plus PCI

statement: VerificationState (ChunkVerified, PhysicalRootVerified, Unverified) is defined with the doc 'reader must carry verification state rather than invite inference' but is never used anywhere in the crate or CLI.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §19.4 L2152 requires verification state carried per Reader result; SPEC §20.5 L2237 UNVERIFIED qualifier
decision_needed: How are per-read verification states surfaced (chunk digest vs Merkle slice vs none), and how do they map to OK+UNVERIFIED?

statement: build_content splits plaintext into fixed-size ranges; chunk_size 0 is POLICY_REFUSED.

build_content_from_ranges computes logical_digest = SHA-256(plaintext) and chunk_id = SHA-256(chunk bytes), deduplicates identical chunks within the object, and treats distinct plaintext with the same chunk id as CORRUPT EB_INTEGRITY_CHUNK_IDENTITY_COLLISION.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §3.5 C2 L271
research_needed: Add a synthetic test for ChunkIdentityCollision (requires injected digest)

statement: Chunk ranges must start at 0, be non-empty, contiguous, non-overlapping and exactly cover the plaintext; otherwise NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_SECTION_STRUCTURE.
Zero-length content yields a ContentObject with no chunks, logical digest SHA-256 of empty input and the domain-separated empty chunk-tree root; the File still carries an Internal ContentRef.
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves SPEC open question §3.2 L152/§3.5 L238 (spec-01-0176)

statement: apply_native_identities validates the model, verifies chunks/content, then recomputes every Entry identity/aux digest, canonicalizes fidelity and conversion lists, clears PCI and writes LAI/PCR/AUX; caller-provided digest placeholders are ignored.

native_identities_from_verified (crate-private) computes identical LAI/PCR/AUX without retained plaintext for STREAM readers, relying on incremental chunk verification; identities use only entry fields, (logical_digest, chunk_root) pairs, (chunk_id, logical_len) leaves and fidelity.

Full verification: each Chunk's length and SHA-256 must match (CORRUPT EB_INTEGRITY_CHUNK_DIGEST_MISMATCH); each ContentObject's streamed SHA-256 over its chunks must equal logical_digest (EB_INTEGRITY_CONTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH) and its chunk_root must recompute (EB_INTEGRITY_CHUNK_ROOT_MISMATCH).
evidence_in_source: code; ChunkDigestMismatch tested tests/native_ecf.rs:370-379; content/chunk-root codes unasserted
research_needed: Add tests asserting ContentDigestMismatch and ChunkRootMismatch

statement: chunk_root is a Merkle root over leaves H('chunk-tree/leaf', chunk_id, u64 logical_len) with 'chunk-tree/empty' and 'chunk-tree/node' domains; it is a bare root (no descriptor) bound later through PCR.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §8.6 L969-972; SPEC open question §8.4 L951 (spec-03-0203) on bare roots persists
decision_needed: Should per-object chunk_root be descriptor-bound for standalone range verification?

statement: Merkle construction: empty list hashes the empty domain; a single leaf is the root itself; otherwise split at the largest power of two below n and hash node(left, right). No padding.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §8.6 L971-972

statement: Entry identity digest: Directory/File use domain entry/identity/v1 over ('identity/v1', encoded path, kind 1|2, content kind 0|1, content digest or empty, identity metadata).
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §8.0 L871 and docs/format-v0.md L393-394

statement: Symlink identity uses domain entry/identity/v2 (kind 3, target encoding byte 1 UTF8 / 2 POSIX_BYTES, exact target bytes); ReparsePoint uses entry/identity/v3 (kind 4, tag u32 BE, exact data). Target and reparse data are LAI facts.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L387-391 domain list omits entry/identity/v2 and v3 (documentation drift)
decision_needed: Update format-v0.md domain list to include entry/identity/v2, v3, hardlink-group, legacy-preservation and aux-preservation domains?

statement: Entry aux digest is H('entry/aux/v1', encoding of all metadata items not participating in identity v1).
refines_or_supersedes: Matches SPEC §8.0 L872

statement: hardlink_group_id = H('entrybound/hardlink-group/v1', content digest, count plus canonically sorted encoded member paths); requires >=2 unique paths and is inode- and traversal-independent.
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves SPEC open question §3.3a (spec-01-0103)
evidence_in_source: code; test identity.rs:1181-1195 with frozen vector e7dad4aa...dc61

statement: verify_metadata_lai recomputes Entry identity digests and LAI from fetched metadata only (no chunk plaintext or physical organization), yielding EB_INTEGRITY_ENTRY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH or EB_INTEGRITY_LAI_MISMATCH; used by ecf/random.rs:241 and crypto/random.rs:419.

verify_metadata_aux hardcodes the conversion-absent digest and ignores LegacyPreservation, so partial AUX verification cannot validate converted or preserved archives; unencrypted INDEXED random access does not verify AUX at all (ecf/random.rs:985 NotRequested).
research_needed: Test encrypted INDEXED random access on a converted (ZIP-imported) archive
decision_needed: Should random-access AUX verification support ConversionProvenance/preservation and be offered for unencrypted archives?

statement: Manifest root is a Merkle tree over H('manifest/leaf', identity_digest) in canonical entry order. LAI = H('lai/v1', 'sha256', manifest root, 'identity/v1', role byte 1 (Complete), u64 entry count, u64 total logical size).
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §8.0 L874/§8.4 L946 and I22; role byte per docs/format-v0.md L398

statement: PCR = H('pcr/v1', 'sha256', count plus digest-ordered (logical_digest, chunk_root) pairs, unique chunk count, chunker_id bytes). Transform plans, codecs, layout and physical order are excluded so recompression with unchanged chunking preserves PCR.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md L400-402

statement: AUX = H('aux/v1', 'sha256', entry-aux Merkle root, H('fidelity/v1', fidelity), conversion digest or H('conversion/absent/v1')); with preservation, AUX = H('aux-preservation/v1', base, H('legacy-preservation/v1', encoding including full source bytes)).
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §8.0 L876/§8.4 L948; aux-preservation wrapper absent from docs/format-v0.md L387-405
research_needed: Measure AUX hashing cost when preserving large legacy sources

statement: Preservation and conversion encodings for AUX: length-prefixed strings, u64 BE counts/ordinals, validity codes 1/2/3, preserved value tags 0 none,1 bytes,2 unsigned,3 signed,4 text,5 boolean, optional resolution/authority presence bytes.

Before hashing, conversion resolutions, synthesized ancestors, unsupported-metadata lists and fidelity captured/filesystem/unavailable/degraded lists are sorted and deduplicated, so duplicate declarations silently collapse rather than being rejected.
decision_needed: Should duplicate fidelity/conversion items be rejected instead of collapsed?

statement: Path encoding for identity: u64 component count, then per component encoding byte 1 (UTF-8) and length-prefixed bytes, so the declared encoding participates in identity.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §8.3 L930 (component bytes and declared encodings); relates to SPEC open question §8.3 (spec-03-0195)

statement: Metadata items are split by identity participation; each is encoded as name string, criticality byte (0 Optional, 1 Critical), restorability byte (1 Restorable, 2 CaptureOnly) and a typed value tag 1-13 (bool, timestamp, mode, uid, gid, hardlink group, xattrs, sparse map, ACLs, SD, file attributes, reparse original, macOS flags).
refines_or_supersedes: Realizes SPEC §10.3 L1246 (optional items covered by digests)

statement: ACL principal identity tags: UserObj 1, User 2+uid, GroupObj 3, Group 4+gid, Mask 5, Other 6, Owner@ 7, Group@ 8, Everyone@ 9, Uuid 10+16 bytes. Timestamp precision ids: Second 1 .. Nanosecond 5.
Fidelity encoding: captured list, unavailable issues, degraded issues (class, reason, optional scoped path), platform string, filesystem list.
Frozen identity tiers test: adding posix.mode or a sparse map changes only aux_digest; changing core.executable changes identity_digest; different symlink targets change identity_digest.

Platform identity tiers test: ACLs, Windows security descriptors and macOS flags change only aux_digest; reparse data changes identity_digest; windows.reparse-original on a Symlink changes only aux_digest.

No Merkle inclusion-proof, slice or MERKLE_OUTBOARD API exists: chunk_root can only be recomputed from the full ordered leaf list, so verifying a byte range against a signed PCR with O(log n) nodes is not implemented.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §8.6 L975-977 and §13.2 L1527 require Merkle-slice verified partial reads
research_needed: Measure proof size and fetch cost for verified ranges over CDC chunk lists
decision_needed: Is MERKLE_OUTBOARD with inclusion proofs V1, or are flat chunk digests plus full leaf lists sufficient?

statement: planner_id is bound into neither LAI nor PCR; chunker_id is bound only into PCR.
Six top-level outcome classes with stable names: OK, UNSUPPORTED, TRUNCATED, CORRUPT, NONCONFORMING, POLICY_REFUSED.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §20.5 L2226 six outcome classes

statement: ReasonCode has 145 variants, each mapped to an EB_-prefixed string; Diagnostic Display renders 'CLASS CODE: detail' and Result<T> aliases Result<T, Diagnostic>.

EB_ECF_* container codes: BAD_MAGIC, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE, TRUNCATED_FOOTER, TRUNCATED_STREAM, INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH, FOOTER_BINDING_MISMATCH, SECTION_STRUCTURE, SECTION_DIGEST_MISMATCH, INDEX_ABSENT/INVALID_REBUILT, DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_DECLARATION, NONCANONICAL_ENCODING, STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING/WINDOW_EXCEEDED/FORWARD_REFERENCE, INVALID_CHUNK_GROUP_ORDERING, ACCESS_COST_MISMATCH.
EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT is the single generic code for format bounds and caller policy limits (usually with POLICY_REFUSED).

EB_EAM_* model codes: DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH, DOT_COMPONENT, DOT_DOT_COMPONENT, INVALID_PATH_COMPONENT, MISSING_ANCESTOR, FILE_AS_ANCESTOR, DIRECTORY_HAS_CONTENT, FILE_MISSING_CONTENT, INVALID_SYMLINK_TARGET, INVALID_POSIX_METADATA, INVALID_HARDLINK_GROUP, INVALID/DUPLICATE_XATTR, INVALID_SPARSE_MAP, INVALID_ACL, INVALID_WINDOWS_SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR, INVALID_WINDOWS/MACOS_METADATA, INVALID_REPARSE_POINT, UNKNOWN_CONTENT_OBJECT/CHUNK/DICTIONARY/TRANSFORM_PLAN, INVALID_CHUNK_GROUP_REFERENCE.

EB_INTEGRITY_* codes: DICTIONARY_DIGEST_MISMATCH, PREREQUISITE_CHUNK_CORRUPT, RECONSTRUCTION_DATA_DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECONSTRUCTION_REGION_MEMBER_DIGEST_MISMATCH, CHUNK_DIGEST_MISMATCH, CHUNK_IDENTITY_COLLISION, CONTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH, CHUNK_ROOT_MISMATCH, ENTRY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, ENTRY_AUX_MISMATCH, LAI/PCR/AUX_MISMATCH.
EB_CODEC_* codes: UNSUPPORTED_DICTIONARY_FORMAT, LOOKBACK_VIOLATION, UNKNOWN, INVALID_PARAMETERS, COMPRESSION_FAILED, DECOMPRESSION_FAILED, DECOMPRESSED_LENGTH_MISMATCH.
EB_TRANSFORM_* codes: UNKNOWN, INVALID_PARAMETERS, FAILED, LENGTH_MISMATCH.
EB_RECONSTRUCTION_* codes: DATA_UNKNOWN, FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, FAILED, LENGTH_MISMATCH, DIGEST_MISMATCH, REGION_UNKNOWN, REGION_OVERLAP, REGION_INVALID, REGION_ACCESS_INVALID, PAYLOAD_MALFORMED.

EB_CRYPTO_* codes: SUITE_UNSUPPORTED, LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED, NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT, RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID, RECIPIENT_POLICY_INVALID, ENVELOPE_AUTH_FAILED, KEY_COMMITMENT_FAILED, PASSWORD_KDF_POLICY_REFUSED, AEAD_AUTH_FAILED, SEGMENT_STRUCTURE_INVALID, PADDING_INVALID, PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID, BOUNDARY_MODE_UNSUPPORTED, RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED.
EB_SIGNATURE_* codes: ABSENT, UNSUPPORTED, INVALID, STALE_CONTENT, STALE_PHYSICAL, STALE_ADDRESSING, TIMESTAMP_INVALID, TIMESTAMP_UNSUPPORTED.

Legacy codes: EB_LEGACY_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED/RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED/EXPORT_LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED/EXPORT_REFUSED/EXPORT_TARGET_INVALID; EB_ZIP_* (9), EB_TAR_* (6), EB_WRAPPER_* (3), EB_7Z_* (7) covering structure, unsupported feature/coder, conflict divergence/irreconcilable, checksum/CRC/size, unsafe path, ambiguous name, overlapping extent.

Input/access/extraction codes: EB_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_ENTRY_KIND, EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE, EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_* (POLICY_REFUSED, NOT_INDEXED, ENTRY_NOT_FOUND, ENTRY_NOT_FILE, DEPENDENCY_INVALID), EB_HTTP_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED/INVALID, EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION, EB_EXTRACT_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE, EB_EXTRACT_UNSAFE_SYMLINK.
Miscellaneous codes: EB_INPUT_NOT_DIRECTORY, EB_CLI_USAGE, EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, EB_IO.

Reason-code string prefixes do not follow enum grouping or subsystem consistently (e.g. InvalidGroupOrdering is EB_ECF_, LookbackViolation is EB_CODEC_, DictionaryDigestMismatch is EB_INTEGRITY_); there are no codes for P5 path collisions, unknown Critical metadata, external references/base chains, parity or salvage.
decision_needed: Should the reason-code taxonomy be reorganized/extended before it is declared version-stable?

statement: Encoding the same in-memory archive twice yields byte-identical output and identities; reopening reproduces the archive and reports canonical encoding, chunk integrity, PCI computed and a valid Index.
mtime changes alter AUX but not LAI; flipping core.executable or changing file content alters LAI.
Re-chunking the same content (1 MiB vs 512 KiB fixed) preserves LAI and AUX while changing PCR.
Omitting or corrupting the Index leaves LAI, PCR, AUX and semantic entries unchanged, reports RebuiltAbsent/RebuiltInvalid with EB_ECF_INDEX_ABSENT_REBUILT/INVALID_REBUILT, and changes only PCI.
For all four compression profiles, INDEXED and STREAM encodings share LAI, AUX, PCR, entries, content store and plans, differ in PCI and bytes, and both extract to trees equal to the source.
Changing chunking changes PCR but not content logical digests or LAI.
Creation profile (planner choice) is physically separate from logical identity.
